purpose: Individual reconciliation against each existing scope. Completed review is not product certification or proof that every gap is resolved.

applications.name: calibre
applications.version: Source commit e2a169f96a30b9be215e3abd78cb0599e7a4479a; populated metadata SQLite relationships and preference-restore conditions
E3: The populated metadata fixture independently exposes book/author/tag/custom-column relationships, and the restore source conditionally reuses a preference backup. Its three database records have no restored book files, covers or comparison for the declared 150-book/conversion-state profile. Neither OPF reconstruction nor the readable database alone establishes complete E3.
E5: Library and device deletion use explicit helper/warning paths, recently deleted restoration exists, and backend expiry can close that recovery window, including an on-close setting. The remaining conversion/metadata overwrites, effective confirmation preferences and restoration after expiry are not sufficiently covered for the existing library scope.
longevity: E3 is not established for calibre's existing essential-record scope. The previous Longevity finding is replaced by Not assessed, not a verified failure or a positive placeholder.
transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.

findings.text: The library-delete action calls a confirmation helper, uses a non-permanent removal path for bulk library deletion and exposes recently deleted restoration. Device deletion has a separate permanent-removal warning. Helper invocation is established, not an unconditional prompt under every saved preference or a successful restore.

Trash expiry is time/preference-dependent, and closing the database explicitly expires trash when the configured expiry is zero. Retention is therefore not a permanent backup or a guarantee that every deleted book remains recoverable.

applications.remaining: A complete library/OPF/prefs restore with book files, covers, annotations and conversion settings; cross-version reopening, DRM limits and destructive deletion. E5 also needs effective deletion/overwrite settings, conversion and bulk metadata mutation boundaries, and recovery evidence before/after trash expiry.
applications.current_remaining: A complete library/OPF/prefs restore with book files, covers, annotations and conversion settings; cross-version reopening, DRM limits and destructive deletion. E5 also needs effective deletion/overwrite settings, conversion and bulk metadata mutation boundaries, and recovery evidence before/after trash expiry.
applications.next: Obtain a synthetic complete library with files/OPFs/preferences and expected metadata/resource hashes; compare it independently and seek version-matched deletion/conversion/expiry observations or comprehensive control-source evidence.
E2: The former E2 Pass does not demonstrate usable migration of custom columns, reading metadata, covers and conversion-state meaning into another library workflow. The available book/database observations leave those essential relationships unestablished.
sovereignty: A positive Sovereignty finding requires established E1, E2 and E4 in the declared scope. The existing access/exit/custody record for calibre does not establish all three minimums. The prior positive finding is withdrawn; recorded storage and portability strengths remain facts, not a verified failure.

findings.text: The autosave timer follows the enable/interval configuration. Its save attempt checks for a current project, needAutoSave and canSave, and logs failure; old temporary autosave material can be removed as the active project state changes. Notation undo/redo delegates to the transaction manager; explicit rollback and commit end transactions with different flags and notify state changes. These are inspectable editing-control entry points, not proof that every plugin, save or exported representation can be rolled back.

The page-view undo stack replays recorded text-buffer actions and can stop recording handlers during blocked changes. This is editor-level undo, not a filesystem snapshot or a guarantee of recovery from page-folder deletion and external synchronization.

applications.name: Taskwarrior
applications.version: Source commit c280c347c1adc47e9bb1ad42c92958e2d7f92e9c; JSON fixture interpretation, export scope and duplicate-UUID import updates
E3: The independently parsed import literals expose five task UUIDs and basic dates/status, while the source exports selected attributes and updates existing UUIDs on import. Full recurrence, annotations, UDAs, dependencies, history and TaskChampion database reconstruction remain unverified; a filtered task listing is not complete profile recovery.
E5: Purge is limited to deleted tasks and uses permission/relation handling; undo previews operations, is confirmation-configurable and can refuse reversal after intervening operations. These controls do not establish effective settings, import/sync/hook authority and complete correction across the existing recurring multi-replica task workflow.

transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.

findings.text: The purge command selects already-deleted tasks and calls the permission path before purging them. Recurrence templates with live children are rejected; dependent-task links can be removed during relation handling. This is not an append-only operation or proof that every setting forces an interactive prompt.

Undo renders the operations and old/new property values to be reverted, requests confirmation unless its setting disables that prompt, and reports if other operations prevent committing the reversal. This does not establish indefinite history, post-sync undo or recovery of every purged payload.
